is.title: Leiðsögn á Árbæjarsafni
is.text: Leiðsögumaður fer með gesti í öll helstu hús Árbæjarsafns og segir frá sögu þeirra. Leiðsögnin fer að mestu fram á ensku og tekur rúma klukkastund.
is.details: Árbæjarsafn er útisafn sem var stofnað árið 1957 en auk Árbæjar eru þar yfir tuttugu hús, sem mynda torg, þorp og sveit. Í Árbæjarsafni er leitast við að gefa hugmynd um byggingalist og lifnaðarhætti í Reykjavík á 19. og 20. öld. Hvert og eitt hús geymir annaðhvort sjálfstæða sögusýningu eða þá að þar er sýnt dæmigert heimili frá ákveðnu tímabili. Á safninu má einnig sjá gamaldags verkstæði ýmiskonar þar sem sjá má dæmigerða aðstöðu, tækni og tól.

en.title: Guided tour at Árbær Open Air Museum
en.text: The guide takes guests to all the main houses of the museum and tells their stories. The guided tour is in English and takes just over an hour.
en.details: Árbær was an established farm well into the 20th century, and the museum opened there in 1957. Árbær is now an open-air museum with more than 20 buildings which form a town square, a village and a farm. Most of the buildings have been relocated from central Reykjavik. The Museum seeks to give an idea of Reykjavik's architecture and way of life in the 19th and 20th centuries. Each house contains an independent historical exhibition or a typical home from a specific period. The museum also houses old-fashioned workshops on typical facilities, technology, and tools.

is.title: Hannyrðastund í Spönginni
is.text:
Ertu með eitthvað á prjónunum? Ertu að hekla fallegt sjal eða sauma út púða?

Á fimmtudögum kl. 13:30-14:30 er hannyrðastund í Borgarbókasafninu Spönginni frá september fram í lok maí. Öll velkomin, byrjendur og lengra komin, í notalega stund í blágrænu sófunum á annarri hæð.

Við spjöllum um daginn og veginn, fáum okkur kaffi og sinnum handavinnunni í góðum félagsskap. 

Við eigum líka mikið úrval af alls kyns bókum og tímaritum um handavinnu sem hægt er að sækja innblástur í og grípa með sér heim.

en.title: Handicraft Time in Spöngin
en.text:
Are you knitting a sweater, crocheting a scarf or working on some beautiful embroidery?

Every Thursday from 1:30 pm - 2:30 pm we have a cozy time together in the blue green couch on second floor in the Spöngin City Library (Grafarvogur neighborhood) from September until the end of May. We work on our things, have some coffee and chat about everything and nothing.

All welcome, beginners and advanced.

is.title: Hannyrða- og bókahittingur í Grófinni
is.text:
Ertu ástríðufullur prjónari eða heklari sem elskar líka að lesa og spjalla um skemmtilegar bækur? Þá er þessi hittingur á bókasafninu eitthvað fyrir þig.

Það er gaman að sameina þessi tvö áhugamál og enn betra að geta hitt góðan hóp sem deilir þessari ástríðu. 
Við komum saman á fimmtudögum á milli kl. 15 og 17 í Hannyrðahorninu á 2. hæð í Borgarbókasafninu Grófinni frá september fram í lok apríl. 

Umsjón með hittingnum hefur Guðrún Dís, áhugasamur nýgræðingur í hannyrðum  sem heldur utan um hópinn, kemur með hugmyndir að skemmtilegu lesefni og leiðir spjallið. 
Ekki er um hefðbundinn leshring að ræða og því þarf ekki að lesa ákveðnar bækur fyrir hvern hitting, aðeins mæta á staðinn og taka þátt í spjallinu. 

Hittingarnir fara fram á íslensku og/eða ensku og tekur mið af samsetningu hópsins hverju sinni.

Engin skráning og þú mætir bara þegar þig langar í félagsskap.

Nánari upplýsingar veitir:
Guðrún Dís Jónatansdóttir, deildarstjóri miðlunar
gudrun.dis.jonatansdottir@reykjavik.is | 411 6115

en.title: Handicrafts & Book Chat in Grófin
en.text:
Do you love knitting or crocheting as well as reading and chatting about good books? Then these meetups are something for you. 

It’s nice to combine those two interests and even better to connect with others who share the same passion. 

We will meet on Thursdays between 3 pm and 5 pm in the Handicraft Corner on the 2nd floor in Grófin from September until the end of April.

Guðrún Dís, amateur knitter, will take care of the meetups, show up with some interesting books and lead the discussion. 

This is not a traditional reading club because you don’t have to read specific books before each meeting. Just show up and take part!  

The meetups can be in Icelandic and/or English, depending on the group. 

No registration needed, just pop in when you are in the mood for good company.

Further information:
Guðrún Dís Jónatansdóttir, Head of Communications
gudrun.dis.jonatansdottir@reykjavik.is | 411 6115

is.title: Púslhittingar
is.text:
Ásamt Hinu íslenska púslsambandi ætlar Borgarbókasafnið í Úlfarsárdal að bjóða upp á púslhittinga á fimmtudagskvöldum.

Hér er tilvalið að taka með sér púsl að heiman og eiga notalega stund í skemmtilegum hópi. Einnig verða nokkur púsl á staðnum fyrir þau sem eru að byrja. Þótt ekki verði púsl sérstaklega fyrir börn á staðnum, er fólki velkomið að taka með sér púsl fyrir börnin sín. Börn verða að vera í fylgd með forráðamönnum. 

Púslhittingarnir eru einnig tilvalið tækifæri fyrir áhugasöm til að skiptast á púslum.

Notaleg stemning verður á safninu og kaffi og te í boði fyrir þau sem vilja.

Endilega lítið við!

en.title: Puzzle Meetups
en.text:
In collaboration with the Icelandic Puzzle Association, the Reykjavík City Library in Úlfarsárdalur will be hosting puzzle meetups on Thursday evenings.

This is a great opportunity to bring a puzzle from home and enjoy a cozy time in a friendly group. There will also be a few puzzles available on site for those who are just getting started. While there won’t be puzzles specifically for children, guests are very welcome to bring puzzles for their kids. Children must be accompanied by their guardians.

The meetups are also a great opportunity for enthusiasts to swap puzzles.

There will be a cozy atmosphere at the library, with coffee and tea available for those who would like some.

See you there!

programmes.sourceFullText:
Do you want to walk around and practice your Icelandic while discovering cool exhibitions and cultural landmarks of Reykjavik city?

Join us for this free Icelandic practice meet-ups and get to know other people who are learning the language too! All levels welcome, also beginners!

We meet on the ground floor of the Reykjavik City Library Grófin (downtown), go over some useful vocabulary with our experienced teachers and have some coffee/tea before going on a little field trip together and get to know our city a bit better.

The guided tours at different cultural institutions are in Icelandic but there will be plenty of support for you to understand!

No need to sign up, just show up!

programmes.title: Space for Authors | Two new Books
programmes.sourceFullText:
Authors Hermann Stefánsson and Haukur Arnþórsson invite you to an literary event at the Reykjavík City Library, Grófin, where they will read from and discuss their new novels. Haukur Arnþórsson recently published his debut novel, Christmas or Not Christmas, while Hermann Stefánsson has just released an new novel title, Lambing.

About Christmas or Not Christmas by Haukur Arnþórsson:
Set between Christmas Eve and St. Stephen’s Day in Seyðisfjörður in 1966, the novel tells the story of a group of young people. Old Iceland encounters new ideas, new music, and new technology. Ships arrive and depart, untangling difficult knots along the way.

The principal narrator is a country boy who works as a messenger at the town’s telephone exchange. Little escapes the notice of the staff there. The exchange operator, who is also the town’s singer, finds herself at a turning point and must make decisions that cannot wait. At Hotel Snæfell, a bewildered intellectual from Reykjavík attempts to drink away unresolved contradictions in his own life and in Icelandic food production. The machine workshop’s ship repairs play a role in the story, the chair of the women’s association takes on new challenges with admirable determination, while a senior civil servant continues in familiar fashion.

Review of Christmas or Not Christmas:
“I have now finished reading Haukur Arnþórsson’s novel Christmas or Not Christmas. It is a good book. A very good one, I would say. It kept us engaged and interested through every chapter because we genuinely cared about the people who appeared in it. I already knew Haukur was a fine writer, capable of sharp commentary and clear, concise writing in his professional field. But he also proves himself to be a remarkable storyteller, with a powerful imagination.” (Þórarinn Hjartarson)

About Lambing:
Lambing is a work of fiction by Hermann Stefánsson, whose narrator responds to the following advertisement on Bland.is:

“Looking for a hardworking hand to help with lambing this spring ...”

I wrote to inquire. The person who replied was Elínóra. She gave me her phone number, and we discussed wages and conditions on the farm over the phone. I got the job.

So I set off on my way.

Of course, the advertisement neglected to mention that the stay would come to resemble sitting beneath a sword suspended by a single horsehair, hanging over people’s heads and liable to fall at any moment, bringing sudden death ...

I had no idea what I had gotten myself into.

I did not know that the farm more closely resembled an ancient Greek tragedy than an ordinary Icelandic sheep farm.

Reviews of Lambing:
“The best book I have read this year.” – Uggi Jónsson

“Few things are more Icelandic than lambing season, and Hermann draws out its mythic yet simultaneously chilling dimensions. The quotation on the book’s cover is far from the usual booksellers’ hype, because when I read it for the third time, I genuinely felt that this could well be the book of the year, perhaps even more than that.” – Ármann Jakobsson

“Hermann is the good shepherd who, like all great writers, finds the stories lurking within society, brings them into the light and into the hands of readers, so that they may carry away the sins of the world.” – Guðmundur Andri Thorsson

Everyone is warmly welcome.

Space for Authors
Writers and poets who are publishing a book and would like to present a new and/or previous work are welcome to reserve space at Reykjavík City Library free of charge. Authors are free to use the space as they see fit, whether for readings (including in collaboration with other authors), book launches, or presentations.

For further information, please contact:
Þorgerður Agla Magnúsdóttir
 Project Manager | Literature and Reading Promotion

programmes.title: Nodebook Quests
programmes.sourceFullText:
Nodebook Quests is a series of adventurous journaling workshops that turn exploration into writing. Each session brings a new quest — leading us out into the city, through the library, or sometimes somewhere much closer: inward.

No writing experience is needed — just bring your curiosity and see where the quest takes you.

For Quest No. 1, the prompt stays a secret until the event. You’ll receive your quest, head on a little mission, and come back to turn what you discovered into words. As the series unfolds, writings created during the quests will be collected into a shared Nodebook publication (with each author’s permission).

👪 Free and open to all ages.
☕ Snacks and coffee will be provided at the venue.

Explore more: nodebook.cc
Instagram: @nodebook.cc

More information:
Martyna Karolina Daniel
Project Manager - Equity and Community Engagement
martyna.karolina.daniel@reykjavik.is

programmes.title: Swap Market | Stickers & Collages
programmes.sourceFullText:
Would you like to trade and get new stickers or collage materials to decorate your journals or sketchbooks? Then you are welcome at the Reykjavik City Library in Árbær!

Participation is free, no registration is required, it’s enough to simply show up.
Tables and chairs will be available to display and browse items, - and coffee for those who want to stay a while and chat.

Perfect for anyone who loves stationery and wants to give their journals or sketchbooks new life.

Heiðrún, an artist and member of the library staff, will be on site if there are any questions. She spent one year on an exchange program in Japan, where she developed a strong passion for stationery. Since then, she has kept journals and decorated them with stickers and collage materials.

For further information, please contact:
Heiðrún G. Viktorsdóttir | specialist
heidrun.greta.viktorsdottir@reykjavik.is

programmes.title: Rachmaninoff Vespers - Kyrja + Yrkja - Vigil for victims of war at Hallgrímskirkja
programmes.sourceFullText:
Vocal ensembles Kyrja and Yrkja together present the spectacular All-Night Vigil of Sergei Rachmaninoff in Hallgrímskirkja, with twenty singers and no conductor.

On All Souls’ Day, November 1st, with summer ending and the light fading, we will gather together to commemorate the dead in a ritual of light and music. Together we remember our loved ones, and we dedicate the concert especially to the victims of war in Ukraine and Palestine.

Kyrja is a male vocal ensemble founded in 2022 with the aim of pushing the limits of choral music. Yrkja is a brand new female vocal ensemble founded in 2025, under the same principles. Both are under the artistic direction of Philip Barkhudarov and Sólveig Sigurðardóttir.

The concert is held in collaboration with Hallgrímskirkja and is a part of the church' Autumn concert series.

programmes.title: Soft Networks - Weekly Community Meetups
programmes.sourceFullText:
Do you feel like you have lost control over your digital life? You want to make changes, but is it all too overwhelming? What if your library could help you understand the invisible systems shaping your digital life and help you reclaim time and agency over your personal data?  
Bring your phone, your questions, expertise, and frustrations and join our soft network of weekly gatherings where learning happens collectively and reciprocally; a format where participants share experiences and knowledge with one another alongside hired experts in phone security and textile artists experimenting with phone sleeping bags. 
Together, we’ll look at privacy settings, app permissions, and the hidden layers of your digital identity—like inferred interests, behavioral categories, and how platforms interpret you. We will help you adjust what you use, share, see, and control. We will also sew customized phone sleeping bags to help us choose when to connect and when to let our phones rest so we can do other precious things. So, bring a fabric you have good memories with for the visible outer layer of your phone sleeping bag; we will provide the signal-blocking Faraday fabric that lines the inside of the sleeping bag! No prior sewing experience is needed. 

Every Wednesday from 21st October to 9th December at 16:00-18:00, in the Reykjavik City Library Grófin - 5th floor. Free and open to all. No need to sign up, just show up!

programmes.title: Icelandic & Fusion Poetry - Writing workshops with Marjón
programmes.sourceFullText:
Join us in making Icelandic language rhymes and resonate with other languages, create phonetic ties and meaning beyond linguistic borders, and deepen our emotional connection with Icelandic in the process. Are you using multiple languages daily in Iceland? Do you know a language that you don’t have the chance to use often? Do you know only a few words in forgotten or made-up languages that you cherish and are very much alive in your mind?
In this fusion poetry workshop, we will select words that we love, in Icelandic or other languages, and explore their poetic meaning to us. At the end of each session, for those willing, there will be space for participants to share and test their ongoing work in a cosy and safe setting.

All levels of Icelandic are welcome, from curious beginners to seasoned users and native speakers. The aim is to break barriers between languages, let your mind connect words from different lands, fuse poetic formats and ideas, and play towards rendering your authentic - and poetic - experience of the Icelandic language, no matter how many words you know.

Marjón is an immigrant writer and poet living between languages in Iceland. She is using scraps of Icelandic, English, French and Spanish to create sharp fusion poetry on the migrant experience. She won the Reykjavík Poetry Slam competition 2025 with "Ég neita", using simple Icelandic words to describe linguistic confusion and isolation.
This project is part of the samljóða - writing workshop series and the samvera project which is co-funded by the immigration fund.

Free, no sign up, just show up!

Each bibliotherapy session has its own theme related to human experience and the challenges of everyday life, such as identity, friendship, change, stress, joy, and hope. Participants will have the opportunity to explore these themes through shared reading, reflection, writing, and conversation.

The sessions form a coherent programme, while each session also stands on its own. Participants are therefore welcome to attend one or several bibliotherapy sessions according to their interests and needs, without any requirement for previous participation or preparation.

The emphasis will be on creating a warm and welcoming environment where people can engage with literature on their own terms, share reflections, and encounter different perspectives. Participation in personal discussions will always be voluntary.

The projet aims to provide an accessible space for literature, dialogue, and wellbeing, while strengthening the library's role as a vibrant community hub.

The bibliotherapy sessions are in relations to workshops and a lecture delivered at Reykjavík City Library in October 2026 by bibliotherapy specialist Bijal Shah.

The bibliotherapy sessions will be led by Esther Ágústsdóttir, literary scholar and teacher, and Elín Bergsdóttir, educational and career counsellor, sociologist, and poet both from the Icelandic School of Literature (Bókmenntaskólinn). Both have attended courses and lectures led by Bijal Shah.

The project is a collaboration between Bókmenntaskólinn and Reykjavík City Library, and is supported by the Icelandic Library Fund (Bókasafnasjóður).

Lunchtime Melodies in November will feature songs by Björgvin Halldórsson, who passed away in April this year and left behind a remarkable legacy of beloved Icelandic popular songs that have become cherished classics for generations. 

Sigvaldi Helgi Gunnarsson was raised in Skagafjörður and took his first steps in music there. From a young age, he has performed both as a solo artist and with bands, entertaining his local community at events such as midwinter festivals, birthdays, weddings, funerals, and many other occasions. In 2015, Sigvaldi Helgi reached the finals of The Voice Iceland. 

In 2024, he released the EP Up North, featuring original songs and lyrics. His motto is: “Music for almost every occasion.” 

At these concerts, Sigvaldi will sing and play guitar, accompanied by Leifur Gunnarsson on double bass, who also serves as the artistic director of the concert series. 

Lunchtime Melodies is a concert series presented by City Library in collaboration with double bassist Leifur Gunnarsson. The series features many of Iceland’s leading musicians and provides Reykjavík residents with an opportunity to gather, meet friends, enjoy live music, and chat with the performers after the concert. 

The primary aim of the series is to bring ambitious, high-quality music into the city’s neighborhoods, allowing people to enjoy it within their own communities and on their own terms.
